TARGET_A01 can sustain effective action under acute fear without necessarily showing an extreme physical stress response [D8-Q1-C05; D8-Q1-C06].

TARGET_A01 is strongly motivated to protect close relationships and avoid disappointing or betraying trusted friends [D6-Q1-C01; D6-Q2-C01].
TARGET_A01 accepts the loss of TARGET_A01's own life when judged necessary to defeat a major threat [D2-Q3-C01].

TARGET_A01 gives substantial weight to preserving friends' trust and loyalty, although evidence does not establish that loyalty always overrides fairness or formal duties [D3-Q1-C01].
TARGET_A01 appears strongly concerned with justice and protection of friends, with possible retaliatory impulses when either is threatened [D1-Q1-C02; D5-Q1-C04].

cognitive_appraisal_model: TARGET_A01 appraises dangerous power primarily by whether an adversary can access it, not by its potential personal benefits [D2-Q1-C01].

Distressing memories can recur involuntarily in response to a specific threat, but TARGET_A01 converts this vulnerability into help-seeking and practiced coping [D7-Q1-C01].

interpersonal_patterns: TARGET_A01 tends to gain peer cooperation through trust, liking, and loyalty rather than fear or threats [D6-Q1-C02].

TARGET_A01 combines cooperation and protectiveness with resistance to being pushed around [D6-Q3-C02].

self_narrative_themes: TARGET_A01 appears to regard capability and significance as compatible with humility rather than inherent superiority [D7-Q2-C01].
TARGET_A01 appears to favor a leadership identity grounded in earned trust and loyalty rather than intimidation [D7-Q2-C03].

situation_behavior_signatures: When a dangerous resource could empower an adversary, TARGET_A01 seeks to secure, hide, or destroy it rather than use it personally [D2-Q1-C01].
When confronted by bullying, TARGET_A01 may answer with direct physical intervention [D8-Q1-C03].

When recurring distress is linked to a recognizable threat, TARGET_A01 seeks training and later applies the learned defense [D7-Q1-C01].
